title: Reader Frame
description: The single shared reader-and-situation model that every planning and prose stage reads from and none may contradict.

reader.description: What the intended reader knows and is asking before opening the document.

prior_knowledge.description: What the reader is assumed to already hold.

standing_question.description: The question the reader carries into the document.

mastered_vocabulary.description: In-group settled terms that are safe to leave undefined.

situation.description: The circumstance that makes the document necessary.

unresolved_tension.description: The gap or friction the document exists to close.

expert_blind_spots.description: Knowledge silently assumed by an expert author; bias toward assuming the reader knows too little.

uncertainty_bias.description: The default lean when audience facts are uncertain.

clarification_needed.description: Empty unless audience facts are missing and must be asked before proceeding.

frame_confidence.description: How firmly the reader-and-situation model is grounded.
